correctness.rationale: The proof directly derives the three mutually orthogonal syndrome supports for Dicke gap >=3, confirms contraction of the three recovery Kraus maps, projects sitewise lowering/raising to calculate the accepted jump coefficient and first-order scalar corrected channel, then computes the exact no-jump hypergeometric amplitudes. Distinct endpoint amplitude ratios prove strict \(D<1\) at interior bath population, while binomial variance gives the quadratic coefficient. Extracted package verifier ran successfully with 1348 rational/combinatorial/full-Kraus checks; such finite checks support but do not prove the all-n theorem. Error terms are at fixed n and restricted to weak gamma. The no-jump dephasing factor is relative to the specified physical GAD Kraus grouping, not invariant under Kraus unravelling changes.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text primary paper arXiv:2609.15924v1 proves first-order GAD correction for a five-qubit Dicke pair and a generic PAQEC theorem; this work does not claim either as original. The present single theorem is an explicit all-size complementary-weight construction whose accepted one-jump throughput has the closed p-independent coefficient \(a(n-a+1)/n\) and whose accepted no-jump coherence (in the specified Kraus grouping) has an exact finite-strength hypergeometric expression, strict intermediate-temperature inequality, and coefficient \((n-2a)^2p(1-p)/(2n)\). Full relevant primary text, older published treatments and published-mathematics searches were checked. Strong implicit-derivability risk from the generic PAQEC scheme is acknowledged; explicit numerical coefficients and strict classification were not located in the inspected source.
residual_risks: The 2026 source generic PAQEC formulas may yield the new coefficients after an unreported specialization; implicit prior derivability cannot be excluded.
An unpublished or unindexed equivalent all-size Dicke filter result might exist; Semantic similarity ranks do not establish global uniqueness.
Some supporting works were not read completely (the 2014 publisher article and later portions of the 2018 OA paper).
The restricted-recovery coefficient is not a claim of unconditional best success probability.

value.rationale: The all-length coefficient and coherence formula answer the motivated hardware-design question of accepted correctable thermal jumps versus irreducible no-jump bath-pattern information for complementary Dicke codewords. The p-independent jump coefficient and \(p(1-p)\)-dependent dephasing identify a nontrivial temperature duality; the strict finite-strength threshold and excitation-gap tradeoff provide an exact natural classification. This is not valued merely for reproducible code or the prior-implied existence of probabilistic QEC. Limits: only this symmetric filter and fixed n; no unrestricted recovery optimum or fault-tolerance promise.
